prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor room receding from a bright foreground to a dark hallway and windowed wall roughly 4 to 7 metres behind a woman who stands about 0.5 to 1.2 metres in front of and below the elevated camera wearer. In frame 1, the woman is on the lower left (~1.2 m away) with a partition directly behind her and a clothes rack ~2.5 to 3 metres to her right; in frames 2 and 3, she steps closer (~0.6 to 0.8 m, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) and bends forward toward a low round glass table below her to pick up a small jar within her reach, before straightening up in frame 4 (~0.8 m) and stepping slightly back to ~1.0 m in frame 5 while holding the jar to her face. Across the sequence, her lower body is cropped at the bottom of the frame, her torso occludes the background floor and blue hamper behind her left side in frames 2–4, and her raised left arm and jar partially occlude her face in frame 5. Compared to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the woman's foreground silhouette and the continuous ground plane from the cluttered shadows and sunlit floor streaks, and shows the partition wall edge on the far left of frames 4 and 5 at ~0.5 m. However, the depth map is unreliable around the transparent glass tabletop in frame 3 (which disappears into the floor depth), over-saturates the top of her head to pure white in frames 2 and 4 despite her torso being closer in frame 3, and blurs fine boundaries around her eyeglasses and the held jar.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the woman in front of the camera wearer (~0.5 to 1.2 metres away) as a pink 'person' mask across all five frames, along with a few small object masks, while omitting the surrounding room layout of walls, clothes rack, and floor. As the woman moves from the lower left in frame 1 (~1.2 m away, angled right) toward the centre in frames 2–4 (~0.6–0.8 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach) and slightly back to the lower right in frame 5 (~1.0 m away, facing the camera wearer), her mask tracks her 2D silhouette and posture shifts from upright to bent-over and back to upright. In frames 4 and 5, small masks appear directly within her hands' reach: the round jar held against her chest in frame 4 (~0.8 m from the camera) and up against her nose/mouth in frame 5 (~1.0 m away), where it partially occludes her lower face while her lower body remains out of view below the bottom edge. While the map makes the exact pixel footprint of the held object in frames 4 and 5 stand out sharply against her torso and face, it provides no 3D distance information and fails to segment large scene elements like the clothes rack (~2.5 m behind her), the blue bag (~1.5 m to her left in frames 3–4), or the glass table below her. It is also heavily unreliable in both mask boundaries and class labels: in frame 1 it merges the dark partition behind her into the 'person' mask and hallucinates a separate pink 'person' sliver on a hanging garment ~2.5 m away, in frame 2 it mislabels a sunlit floor/background patch ~3 m to the right as a 'potted plant', and in frames 4 and 5 it misclassifies the jar as a 'remote' and a 'cell phone'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the woman standing 0.5 to 1.2 metres in front of and below the camera wearer, using yellow lines for her torso, shoulders, arms, and facial landmarks (eyes, nose, ears) and magenta skeletons for her hands against a black background with no scene layout. Facial keypoint positions show her head orientation across the frames: in frame 1 she is in the lower left facing forward-right and looking up toward the camera wearer; in frame 2 she steps closer and looks down; in frame 3 she bends deep to the right with her head facing downward toward the floor/table; in frame 4 she faces forward while looking down at her hands; and in frame 5 she faces and looks toward the camera wearer. Her hand skeletons only appear in frames 4 and 5 when her arms bring the jar within ~0.2 to 0.3 metres of her chest and face (and within ~0.8 to 1.0 m of the camera wearer), whereas in frames 1–3 her forearms and hands are out of view below the bottom frame edge or self-occluded as she reaches down. This map makes her shoulder tilt, torso flexion, and dense finger articulations around the occluded jar in frames 4 and 5 explicit even where dark clothing or glare obscures joints in the RGB image. However, it is unreliable when body parts are cropped or steeply foreshortened: it misses her right arm entirely in frame 2, collapses her bent torso into an inaccurate four-sided polygon without arm skeletons in frame 3, drops her left elbow connection in frame 5, and provides no metric depth or object geometry.
